disclaimer: NOT LEGAL ADVICE. This tracker summarizes publicly available high-level information about firearm and conceal-carry rules in California, Oregon, and Nevada for personal reference only. Laws change, court orders enjoin or restore categories, and local rules apply. Always verify with official statutes, attorney general / DPS guidance, and a licensed attorney before carrying or traveling.

states.name: California
states.permitFramework: Shall-issue CCW after Bruen / SB 2; licensing authorities are county sheriffs / city police chiefs (not DOJ).
states.issuer: County sheriff or city police chief
states.minAge: 21+ (typical for CCW; verify with issuing authority)
states.reciprocityIn: California does not honor or recognize CCW licenses issued by other states.
states.reciprocityOutNote: Whether other states honor a CA CCW is up to those states; verify before travel.
states.nonResidentNote: As of Jan 1, 2026, AB 1078 created a statutory path for non-residents to apply for a California CCW (not reciprocity — they must complete CA's application process). See OAG bulletin 2026-DLE-03.
keyRestrictions: Many SB 2 'sensitive places' under PC 26230 — litigation has enjoined some categories historically; private-commercial 'vampire rule' default was struck/enjoined (Wolford-related / Ninth Circuit)
Parks, alcohol-serving establishments, libraries, and stadiums are often cited among enforceable categories
VERIFY: Check current PC 26230 text and live court status before relying on any category list
states.travelerTip: Out-of-state permits are not valid for concealed carry in CA. Unloaded, secured interstate transport may have federal safe-passage protections — verify FOPA and CA rules.
states.possessionNotes: High-level only: CA has extensive possession, magazine, and roster rules beyond CCW. This tracker covers carry framework only — not assault-weapon, magazine-capacity, or roster law.

states.name: Oregon
states.permitFramework: Shall-issue Concealed Handgun License (CHL) via county sheriff under ORS 166.291; not constitutional carry.
states.openCarryNote: Open carry without a CHL is generally lawful under state law but local restrictions (esp. loaded carry in some cities) can apply — check locality.
states.reciprocityIn: Oregon does not recognize concealed carry licenses from any other state. An Oregon CHL is required to carry concealed.
states.nonResidentNote: Residents of contiguous states may be able to apply for an Oregon CHL (county practice varies); residents generally apply in county of residence.
keyRestrictions: Statutory and posted prohibited locations — verify ORS and local ordinances
Local loaded-carry restrictions may apply even where open carry is otherwise lawful
states.travelerTip: Out-of-state permits are not recognized for concealed carry in Oregon. Obtain an Oregon CHL if you need to carry concealed.
states.measure114Note: Measure 114 (permit-to-purchase / related rules) has been in litigation; effective date has been delayed (reports cite Jan 1, 2028 push). Track separately from CHL — do not conflate with CHL.
states.possessionNotes: High-level only: CHL framework is separate from Measure 114 permit-to-purchase litigation. Verify both tracks independently.

states.name: Nevada
states.permitFramework: Shall-issue Concealed Firearm Permit (CFP) via county sheriff. NOT permitless/constitutional carry for concealed carry.
states.reciprocityIn: Nevada recognizes permits from states on the DPS RCCD recognition list (updated periodically, often July 1).
states.important: CA and OR are NOT on Nevada's recognition list (as of the July 1, 2026 list). New Nevada residents with an out-of-state permit must get a Nevada county permit within 60 days (NRS 202.3688).
states.openCarryNote: Open carry without a permit is generally allowed for eligible persons, but concealed carry without a recognized permit is a serious crime under NRS 202.350.
keyRestrictions: Other statutory and posted locations — verify NRS and local rules
states.travelerTip: If your home-state permit is on the NV DPS recognition list, concealed carry may be allowed under that recognition — verify the current PDF list. CA and OR permits are not recognized.
states.possessionNotes: High-level only: Concealed carry without a Nevada or recognized permit is a serious crime. Open carry rules differ — do not conflate.
